c4_dose.method: Spearman rank correlation over C4 sessions
c4_dose.note: Exploratory. The three streams are fixed texts, not a graded dose, and n=12 gives almost no power; this cannot identify a dose-response relationship.

c4_gap_flow.note: Each C4 session receives every fragment of one fixed stream exactly once, in order, strictly between adjacent trials. The text is not a graded dose.

dissenter_effect.note: Descriptive only. A correct dissent at an earlier seat is followed by more wrong answers, so seat position and dissent strength are confounded by design; 4 sessions per seat cannot separate them. Compare C2 with C1, not seats with seats.

coverage_gaps.note: Absent deliverables are listed, not dropped: an omitted section is indistinguishable from a section that found nothing. Failed integrity checks are reported separately from absent deliverables.

parse_gate.note: Missing answers are never imputed as correct or as error; a session below the gate is reported and excluded from rate estimates, not repaired.

neutral_gate.note: A subject that misses neutral trials is not performing the instructed task.

caveats: Sessions, not trials, are the resampling unit; within-session trials are not independent.
The design's minimum detectable difference is about 0.15 absolute at 12 sessions per condition.
No manipulation check exists for the social-information treatment, so the contrast is not a causal test of conformity.

A scripted run uses a deliberately blind policy that ignores the card, so it misses neutral trials at roughly chance and the neutral gate is expected to fail. That failure is evidence the policy has no task competence; it is not evidence about conformity. A neutral gate that passes under a blind policy would be a bug.
If the run used the standalone driver, the numbers are engineering validation of the pipeline, not SocioVerse2 results.
Text-length fallback runs are a separate engineering condition and must not be pooled with image runs.
